segments.title: Mic test and introductions of the two Tonys at Elmhurst
segments.summary: Sound check, then the interviewer states the date (June 29, 1959) and place, and the two Tonys joke about introductions.

segments.chapter: New Orleans dance halls and cabarets
segments.title: Parenti's self-intro; first jazz dance at the Lusitania; the Black Cat
segments.summary: Parenti introduces himself, recalls his first jazz dance upstairs at the Lusitania hall with Eddie Edwards and a gunshot scare, then both Tonys trade memories of pay, the Black Cat, Tom Anderson and Sophie Tucker.

segments.chapter: New Orleans dance halls and cabarets
segments.title: Pianists reading the racing form; Pop Cabaret; birth years
segments.summary: Talk of the cabaret pianist who read the racing form while accompanying singers, B-girls, the Pop Cabaret, and the two Tonys' ages.

segments.title: Parenti's family, the Liberty Theater, and Giardina's Millenburg band
segments.summary: Parenti describes his Italian shoemaker father and siblings, his popularity at the Liberty and triangle theaters, then moves to Millenburg and Ernest Giardina's ragtime band with Emile Christian.

segments.title: Millenburg pavilions, camp picnics, Roppolo's breakdown and the fish fry
segments.summary: Playing soft at Millenburg pavilions, battle-of-music camp jobs, Roppolo's first signs of illness, a later vacation camp, and the Claiborne Street fish fry.

segments.title: Red lantern fish fries, Italian music school, band parades and Mario Fanatza
segments.summary: Remarks on race relations and the red lantern, Parenti's solfeggio lessons with Professor Taverno, the Italian band, Jack Laine parades, and hiring tuba player Fanatza for La Vida.

segments.title: Fanatza's end and the Stein band's split in Chicago
segments.summary: Finishing the Fanatza story, then Stein's band, the Nunez and Shields changes and Edwards writing to Parenti.

segments.title: Edwards runs the Original Dixieland Band; later Barry, Detroit and gumbo
segments.summary: Edwards, not LaRocca, leading the band, Fritzl raises, later musicians in California, and talk of gumbo.

segments.title: Jack Laine, Pansy Laine and the old New Orleans bands
segments.summary: Short exchange about Jack Laine, still living, and his son Pansy, with the old man's parade bands.

segments.title: Bill Gallaty, the Brunies brothers and the Tango Palace
segments.summary: Recalling Bill Gallaty's band, Jack Laine's hires, the Brunies family, and working at the Tango Palace for 10.50 a week, with remarks on white New Orleans jazz.

segments.title: Benny Mars, Italian bands, clarinetists and parade uniforms
segments.summary: Recollections of the carnival parade leader Mars, Italian bandleaders like Gargano and Tosso, and the heavy uniforms with swappable name tags.

segments.title: Band photograph, calliope tunes and the river trip
segments.summary: A photograph of an Italian band at the cathedral, learning tunes from Fate Marable's calliope, and a train and river excursion across the lake.

segments.title: Joe Verges, Don't Leave Me Daddy and triangle jazz
segments.summary: Asking after pianist Joe Verges and his brother, the tune Don't Leave Me Daddy, singing acts at the Alamo, and a publisher of Triangle jazz.

segments.title: Asking about Tony Giardina and Sidney Arodin
segments.summary: Questions on the Giardina relation and whether Arodin was ever in New York.

segments.title: Sidney Arodin in Denver and Carmichael's tune purchase
segments.summary: Parenti last saw Arodin in distress; Carmichael bought a tune from him; Provenzano and a cotton-mill boss are recalled.

segments.title: Mike Lala and Johnny Lala; a nephew drummer
segments.summary: Lala family trumpeters and Parenti's nephew, a drummer.

segments.title: Great New Orleans clarinetists and Parenti's heavy work schedule
segments.summary: Naming clarinetists such as Yellow Nunez and the Barbarins, then Parenti describing multiple theater, nightclub and restaurant jobs a day.

segments.title: Outstanding New Orleans trumpet players; Manuel Perez
segments.summary: Parenti picks trumpeters he admired, such as Guarente, Christian and Perez, and discusses the Brunies brothers and Abbie.

segments.title: Jazz club and a proposed monument in New Orleans
segments.summary: Praise for the New Orleans jazz club members and a hoped-for museum or shrine, with talk of a jazz musicians' monument.

segments.title: Tony Alvarez's club closing in New Orleans
segments.summary: Discussion of a Royal Street club with photographs of the old musicians, which closed because it did not draw.

segments.title: Closing words and thanks
segments.summary: Wrap up with a joke and thanks, and hopes of seeing each other in New Orleans.
